name: Archaeological Ensemble of Mérida
description: Mérida, in western Spain's Extremadura region, began in 25 BC as Augusta Emerita, a colony for retired Roman legionaries that grew into the capital of Lusitania. Today you can walk across a long Roman bridge over the Guadiana, sit in the ancient theatre and amphitheatre where gladiators once fought, and see the remains of a huge chariot circus and the aqueducts that supplied the city.
